subject: PraxisWorks adapter compatibility & lab test plan
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@praxisworks.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sara.nguyen@praxisworks.com
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PraxisWorks — Redwood adapter compatibility and test plan

Hi Sergio / Marissa,

Thanks again for the initial call yesterday. As discussed, our team has finished the first pass at the PraxisWorks adapter for Redwood's serving API. We'd like to run a short compatibility validation in your partner lab next week to confirm:

- TLS / mutual auth behavior when deployed to Redwood Dedicated
- Token exchange and ID mapping (we use a custom header X-PW-User)
- Latency profile for typical request sizes (avg 256 token responses)
- Failure modes (backend timeouts, KV cache misses)

I've attached a compatibility matrix (praxis-compat-matrix.csv) and a short YAML of testcases (praxis-testcases.yml). Proposed window: Tuesday, Aug 25 — 2h block (engineering cross-check + smoke runs). Can your team host that slot and can we get a short checklist of preconditions?

Also: we need to confirm whether the Redwood sandbox supports mTLS cert rotation for long-running sessions. If there's a standard runbook or security checklist you prefer, please send it.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Partner Engineering, PraxisWorks
Emma.Li@praxisworks.com
+1 415-555-0126

Attachments: praxis-compat-matrix.csv (csv), praxis-testcases.yml (yml)

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Emma Li <emma.li@praxisworks.com>, Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@praxisworks.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-16T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PraxisWorks — Redwood adapter compatibility and test plan

Emma — thanks for the artifacts. We're good to run a 2-hour lab on Tue Aug 25 14:00-16:00 PT. High-level scope we propose:

1) Preflight (30m) — ensure mutual TLS handshake, validate token mapping header, verify trace propagation.
2) Smoke (30m) — sample inference requests, check correctness and basic latency.
3) Load & stability (40m) — modest sustained throughput (20 rps) to observe batching behavior and KV-cache warmup.
4) Failure injection & recovery (20m) — backend timeout simulation and cache eviction behavior.

Marissa — can you attach our standard partner runbook and confirm lab stack (Dedicated sandbox with GPU VMs + mTLS CA available)? Karthik — would you own orchestration and failure-injection tooling?

Preconditions we'll need from PraxisWorks:
- Access to a test service account (JWT) or static API key that maps to X-PW-User for the test tenant
- A short list of 6 canonical prompts / payload sizes (we can reuse the yaml but call out the 256/512 token cases)
- Confirmation if you will run adapter in a sidecar mode or as an external endpoint (for routing/fallback checks)

I'll drop the calendar invite once we confirm. We'll keep the session recorded and capture per-token latency breakdown from the Console.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: praxis-compat-matrix.csv

From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@praxisworks.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@praxisworks.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PraxisWorks — Redwood adapter compatibility and test plan

Sergio / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from PraxisWorks side:

- We'll run the adapter as an external endpoint behind our ingress (not a sidecar).
- For auth we'll provide a short-lived JWT during the lab; can Redwood accept bearer tokens and still validate X-PW-User mapping?
- mTLS: we can support mutual TLS, but we need to confirm rotation policy / CA chain requirements from your side.

Sara will be the on-call engineer during the test (cc'd). Also, small ask — can Redwood share the expected prefix and length for any cache keys we might emit so we can align cache-invalidation tests?

Carlos Vega
Director, Integrations — PraxisWorks
Carlos.Vega@praxisworks.com

[Attachment: none]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@praxisworks.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@praxisworks.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-17T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PraxisWorks — Redwood adapter compatibility and test plan

Carlos / Emma — answering the bullet points and adding runbook pointers.

- Auth & mapping: Redwood can accept bearer JWTs. We support a configurable header transform rule; we can map your JWT subject to X-PW-User during the lab. We'll need the test JWT or a compliant introspection endpoint.
- mTLS: sandbox supports mTLS. Rotation: our CA rotation window is typically 30 days in sandbox but we can support short lifetimes for test certs. We'll provide the CA bundle before the session.
- Cache keys: primary kv cache keys use the prefix "rw_kv_" and are followed by a 16-char hex digest; for the lab you can expect the pattern rw_kv_<hex>. We'll share a small script to verify eviction.

I've attached the partner runbook (redwood-runbook-v3.pdf) which includes:
- Lab environment topology (Dedicated sandbox + 2 GPU nodes)
- mTLS cert exchange steps
- Failure-injection playbook (curl timeouts, synthetic latency)

Proposed test tracks (to make the 2h efficient):
- Track A (smoke + auth) — ensure handshake, mapping, simple correctness (30m)
- Track B (load + batching) — 20 RPS sustained for 15m, observe batching and token-cost metrics (45m)
- Track C (failure injection & recovery) — simulate backend timeouts and force cache eviction (30m)

We also recommend a short post-test readout (15m) to capture action items.

I'll create the calendar invite and include the drive link with the runbook and scripts. Sergio — assigning Karthik to own orchestration and the failure-injection scripts (karthik_iyer@redwood.ai).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Partner Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-runbook-v3.pdf

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Emma Li <emma.li@praxisworks.com>, Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@praxisworks.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-18T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PraxisWorks — Redwood adapter compatibility and test plan

Emma / Carlos — summary and next steps.

Thanks for confirming the architecture. To summarize the agreed items:
- Lab date: Tue Aug 25, 14:00-16:00 PT (2h). I'll send the calendar invite and include the meeting recording permissions.
- Pre-reqs from PraxisWorks: test JWT or introspection endpoint, confirmation adapter endpoint (external), and the canonical prompts list from the yaml.
- Redwood will provide: mTLS CA bundle, partner runbook (attached by Marissa), cache-key verification script, and orchestration + failure-injection scripts (Karthik owner).

Action owners:
- PraxisWorks: provide test JWT + endpoint details (Carlos / Emma) by EOD Aug 20.
- Redwood: create calendar invite and share drive folder, Karthik to prepare scripts by Aug 22.
- All: 15m readout after the lab to capture any follow-ups.

Karthik — please confirm you can own the orchestration and post-test logs collection.

Looking forward to the session.

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
